transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this. 

I'm just here because... well, I've been having a bit of a hard time lately with my work. I manage IT and information systems, and I keep getting these... thoughts, I guess you'd call them. It's probably silly, but I get terrified that if I miss just one setting, or one access rule, or a warning sign on the network, that someone could get hurt. Or that people could lose absolutely everything. 

And, I mean, part of me knows it’s irrational—I have a graduate degree, I know how these systems actually work—but it just hits me so hard, like I’m personally responsible for preventing some massive disaster. And I just... I can’t seem to just move on from it like a normal person would. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or doing something to try and relieve these thoughts of disaster?

Yeah... um, yes, exactly. It's like you read my mind. I do, um... I do check things. I mean, in my role, being thorough is a good thing, right? You want your IT manager to be careful. But... well, I guess I might be taking it a bit too far. 

I don't want to sound completely unhinged, but I'll find myself rereading our deployment plans, or the network audit logs, just... over and over again. And it bleeds into other things, too, like checking the door locks, or even rereading old messages. Sometimes I, um... I count through the steps in my head while I do it, just waiting for this specific feeling that things are 'safe.' 

I know it sounds ridiculous. I'm really embarrassed to even admit this out loud, but I’ve actually been staying at the office for hours after everyone else goes home. I try to leave on time, I really do, but if I try to stop before that checking process feels complete, I just start to panic. 

Is that... does that sound like something you've heard before? I hope I'm not wasting your time with all this.
Are these checking behaviors and the time you spend on them affecting your relationships or daily life outside of work?

Well... I try really hard to keep it under wraps, you know? I don't want to be a burden to anyone, and I really want to be reliable. But... I guess it is starting to spill over a little bit. 

I hope it's okay to admit this, but I actually missed a major cloud migration deadline recently. I just... I couldn't finish signing off on the final decisions because I was so stuck in that loop of checking everything. My team is wonderful, they really are, but I've noticed they've started sort of... working around me, instead of relying on me for things. Which makes me feel terrible, because I want to be a good manager for them. I'm really trying.

And as for my personal life... um, I've kind of taken a step back from my regular stuff. I used to play basketball, and I went to these salsa nights, which I loved. But I just haven't been showing up lately. I'm usually stuck at the office, or I'm just too completely drained by the time I get home. So I guess I’m losing those routines, and the people that used to keep me grounded. 

I know I shouldn't let it get this far, and I really want to fix it. Does that... I hope that answers your question? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you experience excessive worry or fear in situations that have nothing to do with your work or IT responsibilities?

Um... no, not really. I mean, not that I've noticed, anyway. I'm pretty sure it's almost entirely tied to my job and those systems. 

I guess I'm generally a pretty careful person—I like to make sure things are done right, you know? But I don't think I have those same intense fears or... or that need to constantly check things when I'm just out living my life, or at least not in a way that feels overwhelming. It really just seems to flare up when I'm dealing with work stuff and the responsibility I have there. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not missing something important that I should be telling you. I want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture.
Do you ever feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors outside of work to prevent harm or bad things from happening?

Um... no, I don't think I do. I mean, besides what I mentioned earlier about sometimes checking the door locks at home, but... well, I feel like that's just me being a little overly cautious, right? It's not like I'm doing a whole ritual to stop a disaster from happening. It's just a quick habit to make sure the house is secure. 

But other than that, no, nothing really comes to mind outside of work. I try really hard to just be, you know, normal when I'm not at the office. I don't have any specific routines or things I feel forced to do to prevent bad things from happening, at least not that I've noticed. 

Does that... is that the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions correctly and giving you what you need.
Do you have recurring, intrusive thoughts that are not related to your work or IT responsibilities?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I might worry about normal things every now and then, like anyone else, but I don't have those... those constant, intrusive thoughts about other stuff. It really is just focused on the servers and the network configurations. 

I try to keep a pretty positive mindset outside of work, you know? I don't want to be one of those people who's always stressed out about everything. So, no, I don't think I have thoughts like that about other areas of my life. 

Is that... I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I hope that helps you understand my situation better. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so we can figure this out.
How distressed do you feel when you have these intrusive thoughts about the servers and network configurations?

Um... well, it's... it's pretty bad, honestly. I try to manage it, I really do, but... when those thoughts hit, it's a lot. 

It's like... I keep getting these thoughts that if I miss just one setting, or one access rule, or a warning sign on the network, someone could get hurt. Or they could lose everything. And even though part of me knows it’s irrational—like, I know it doesn't make total sense—it hits me so hard. It feels like I’m personally responsible for keeping everyone safe, and I just... I can’t just move on from it. It really weighs on me.

I hope I don't sound completely crazy saying that. I know it's probably an overreaction, but the distress is... it's pretty intense. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it in a way that's helpful for you.
Do you ever find yourself mentally replaying conversations or interactions you've had with others, going over what was said or what you should have said?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I might think about a conversation for a minute if it was important, but I don't... I don't sit there and replay it over and over. I think I'm pretty good at just letting things go when it comes to talking with people. 

I try to be a good listener and communicate clearly, so I don't usually feel like I need to second-guess what I said or what they said. I just kind of trust that the conversation went how it was supposed to. 

Is that... is that normal? I mean, I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I handle things. I'm doing okay with these questions, right?
Do you feel compelled to do anything specific outside of work to prevent harm or bad things from happening to yourself or others?

Um... outside of work? No, not really. I mean, I try to make sure the doors are locked at home, like anyone would, but it's not... it's not a big thing. 

But, um... at work, or related to work... I guess I do have some things I do. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing a good job, you know? Being thorough. So I'll, um, I'll reread deployment plans and audit logs... a lot. And I check the server room door locks. And sometimes I even go back through old messages over and over. 

I kind of... I count through the steps in my head, just to make sure everything is covered until it feels... safe, I guess. And sometimes... well, sometimes I stay at the office for hours after everyone else has gone home. I just... if I try to stop before it feels complete, I start to panic. I just want to be a reliable manager, you know? 

I hope that doesn't sound too extreme. I just take my responsibilities really seriously. Is it... is it okay that I do that? I mean, I'm just trying to make sure everything is secure. I hope that's the kind of information you needed.
Have you noticed any significant impact on your overall well-being or ability to function in your daily life due to these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors?

Um... well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I'm still coming into the office every day, so I'm functioning, right? But... I suppose it has gotten a bit... complicated. 

I try really hard to keep everything running smoothly, but... well, there was this major cloud migration deadline recently, and... I missed it. I just couldn't bring myself to sign off on the final decisions until I was absolutely sure everything was perfect. And now... I think my team has started just kind of working around me, instead of coming to me for approvals. I know they're just trying to keep the projects moving, but it feels... not great. 

And, um... outside of work... I used to play basketball with some guys, and I went to salsa nights, but I've kind of... stopped showing up for those. I just don't have the time or energy anymore with how late I stay at the office. It's a shame, because those things really used to keep me grounded, and I miss the people. 

But I'm sure it's just a phase, right? Like, once we get past this busy season, things will go back to normal. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I'm still trying my best. Is that... does that answer your question okay? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of details.
Do you feel like you have to perform your checking behaviors in a very specific way or order to feel like they are done correctly?

Um... a specific order? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't have a rigid checklist or anything like that. 

I just... I just check things until I feel like I've done a thorough job, you know? Like, I might look at the logs, and then the deployment plan, or maybe the other way around. It really just depends on what I'm working on that day. I don't feel like I *have* to do it in a certain sequence to make it count. I just want to make sure I'm not missing any details, because that's what a good manager does, right?

I hope that makes sense. I don't want you to think I'm, like, obsessed with routines or anything. I'm pretty flexible about how I get my work done. Is that... is that a good thing? I mean, I hope that's the right answer. I'm really trying to be helpful here.
Are your checking behaviors specifically intended to prevent something terrible from happening?

Um... terrible? I mean... I wouldn't use the word *terrible*. That sounds so dramatic, doesn't it? I just... I just want to make sure I'm doing things right. 

Like I mentioned before, I'll go through the deployment plans, and the audit logs, and... and make sure the server room door locks are secure. And I'll reread old messages, you know, just to be absolutely certain I didn't miss a critical detail. And I do count through the steps in my head, just... just until it feels safe. Like I've covered all my bases. 

I don't think it's about preventing some huge catastrophe... it's just about being responsible. Though, I guess... if I try to leave the office or stop checking before that 'safe' feeling hits, I do start to panic a little. Like my chest gets tight, and I just *have* to stay. Sometimes for hours after everyone else is gone. 

But I'm just trying to be thorough, you know? To protect the company's data. That's a good quality for an IT manager to have, right? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm crazy or anything. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. Does that make sense?
Have your symptoms been causing you significant distress or problems in your relationships, work, or daily activities?

Um... well, I know we kind of touched on this a little bit earlier, and... I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or failing at my job, because I do try so hard. But... yes, I suppose it has been causing some problems. 

I think I mentioned that major cloud migration deadline? I... I ended up completely missing it. I just kept going over the plans, and I couldn't bring myself to actually sign off on the final decisions. It just didn't feel right yet. And now, my team... they've kind of started working around me. Like, they don't come to me for approvals as much anymore. I know they're just trying to be helpful and keep things moving, but it... it makes me feel like I'm letting them down. 

And, um... my personal life has definitely taken a hit, too. I used to really look forward to playing basketball with the guys, and I loved going to salsa nights, but... I've just stopped showing up. I'm usually stuck at the office too late anyway, but even when I'm not, I just don't have the energy. It's tough, because I'm losing those routines and... and the people that used to keep me grounded. 

I'm really trying to get back on track, though. I don't want you to think I've just given up. I'm still coming to work every day and doing my best. Is that... does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm not making it sound too awful. I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
How much time would you say you spend on these checking behaviors each day?

Um... time? Gosh, I... I really couldn't give you an exact number. I've never actually timed it or anything. 

I mean, a lot of it just sort of blends into my regular work, you know? Because reviewing audit logs and going over deployment plans... that's technically part of my job anyway. So it's really hard to separate out what's just me being a diligent manager and what's... you know, the extra checking. 

I know I mentioned staying late sometimes, but I don't want you to think I'm just... paralyzed or wasting the whole day. I'm still working hard. It just takes a little longer to feel completely sure about everything. 

So, I guess I really don't know how much time it adds up to. I hope that's an okay answer? I just don't want to guess a number and have it be wrong, or make it sound way worse than it actually is. I'm really trying to be accurate for you... is that alright?
Have you noticed any significant problems in your relationships with friends, family, or colleagues due to your checking behaviors and thoughts about work?

Um... well, I know I kind of touched on this a few minutes ago, so I hope it's okay if I repeat myself a little bit. I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But, yes... with my colleagues, things have definitely gotten a little awkward. Like I was saying about missing that major cloud migration deadline—because I just couldn't get myself to finish signing off on the decisions—my team has really started working around me. They just don't rely on me the way they used to. I mean, they're a fantastic team, and I know they're just trying to keep the department running smoothly, so I don't blame them at all! But... it does feel like a gap has grown between us, and I feel awful about it. 

And then with my friends... yeah, it's like I mentioned with the basketball games and salsa nights. I've just completely stopped showing up. I feel terrible, because I really don't want to be a bad friend. But because I'm not going, I'm losing those routines, and... and the people that always used to keep me grounded. I'm really trying to figure out how to reconnect with them, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just pushing everyone away on purpose or that I don't care. 

Does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples.
Have you felt like you're unable to fulfill your role as an IT manager due to these intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors?

Um... well, I know we've kind of circled around this a bit already, and I really, really don't want to sound like I'm totally failing at my job... because I do care so much about it. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has made it really hard to fulfill my role lately. 

Like I mentioned before about that cloud migration deadline... I just couldn't get myself to finish signing off on the final decisions, and we ended up missing it. And because of that, my team... they've kind of started working around me. They don't rely on me for approvals the way a team really should rely on their manager. I mean, they're just being proactive, which is great, but... it does make me feel like I'm not doing what I'm supposed to be doing for them.

And it's bleeding into everything else, too. I've stopped showing up for my basketball games and salsa nights, which... I know I already said that, but it just means I'm losing those routines and the people that used to keep me grounded and energized. 

I'm really trying to push through it and get back to being the manager my team deserves. I promise I'm not just giving up. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture.
Have you considered taking a leave of absence from work due to the distress caused by your intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors?

Um... a leave of absence? Oh, wow. No, I... I haven't really considered doing that. 

I mean, I know I just said I've been struggling a bit, but I really don't want you to think it's gotten to the point where I need to just stop working completely. I'm still showing up every day, and I'm really trying my absolute best to push through it and get my work done. 

Honestly, the thought of taking time off... I feel like that would just be letting my team down even more, you know? I'd hate for them or my directors to think I can't handle my responsibilities or that I'm just abandoning them when things get tough. I really want to prove that I can get back on track and be a good manager. 

So, no, I haven't looked into taking a leave. Do you... do you think that's something I *should* be doing? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way, and I value your opinion so much, but I'd really, really prefer to keep working if that's alright?
Do you feel like your checking behaviors have to be done in a way that feels 'just right' or symmetrical to you?

Um... "just right"? I guess... well, I wouldn't want to make it sound like I'm completely rigid or anything, but... yeah, there is a certain way things need to feel before I can move on. 

I really hope this doesn't sound too strange, but when I'm looking at things—like the deployment plans or audit logs, or even just checking the door locks or rereading old messages—I have to go over them again and again. And sometimes... sometimes I count through the steps in my head. I just... I do it until it feels "safe," if that makes sense? 

I know it probably sounds a bit excessive, and I'm really trying to get better about it, I promise. But if I try to stop before it feels complete, I just... I start to panic. It's actually why I've been staying at the office for hours after everyone else leaves. I just want to make sure I'm doing a thorough job and that everything is perfectly secure. 

Does that... does that sound like what you mean by "just right"? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you.
Are you finding it difficult to maintain your personal relationships or daily routines outside of work due to your intrusive thoughts and checking behaviors?

Um... yeah, I know I touched on this a little bit earlier, and I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much... I just want to make sure I'm being helpful. 

But, yes, outside of work, it has gotten a bit difficult. Like I was saying before... I've stopped showing up for my basketball games and my salsa nights. I really don't want to sound like I'm just giving up on my friends or isolating myself, because I'm truly not trying to. It's just... well, because of everything, I'm losing those routines and the people that used to keep me grounded. 

And I know you asked about my personal life, but it really feels like it's all connected to how things are going at the office. Like I mentioned, because I couldn't finish signing off on decisions and missed that major cloud migration deadline, my team has started working around me instead of relying on me. So even my relationships with them feel a bit strained right now. 

I'm really trying my absolute best to get back to my normal schedule, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm just letting my whole life fall apart. Does... does that answer your question? I hope I gave you the right information.
